column1: # SCOPE WORKSHEET, 2026-10-30. The 34 tier-2 case rows owed a `scope_taxid`: every row
# whose assay carries more than one claim-scope taxid in `target.scope_taxids`. One read
# per row, from the row's OWN source paper (not the design paper): which lineage did the
# positives in that paper belong to? Put the taxid in `scope_taxid` here and in the case
# file. `claim_scope_taxa` is how many taxa the design paper claims, which is the size of
# the gap between what the paper asserts and what it showed.
# Leave a row blank if the paper does not say, and say so -- a guessed lineage is worse

column6: source

10.1186/s12917-019-2028-0 Kolesnik 2019: head-to-head of L-gene PCRs for ferlaviruses; Tong's pan-Paramyxovirinae (PAR) set, the one in this entry, was dropped because "we were unable to detect ferlaviral RNA from any genogroup with it". The 29.5% sensitivity and type A/tortoise-only result in that paper are Tong's RMH set (their PCR II), a different assay
10.1186/s12917-019-2028-0 Kolesnik 2019: same paper; this is the PAR-F2/PAR-R semi-nested round of the same PAR set, so the row is not independent of the round1 row
10.1038/s41598-025-03903-x Nesti 2025: adopted Tong's semi-nested primer groups with only indexing and inosine changes and recovered seven novel paramyxovirus sequences from 135 Indonesian bats

10.3389/fpubh.2020.555013 Wacharapluesadee 2020: the pan-CoV PCR returned a positive within 12 h from a traveller from Wuhan, giving a 290 bp sequence 100% identical to SARS-CoV-2 - the first COVID-19 case outside China

10.3390/v13101975 Drzewnievska 2021: reviewed 100 CoV surveillance studies and tested protocols in silico and in vitro; most pan-CoV protocols including this one are strongly biased toward alpha- and beta-CoVs. Entered as partial: the gap is genus scope, not drift

10.3390/v16040534 Wacharapluesadee 2024: head-to-head of three pan-CoV assays on 141 specimens; this one failed to detect delta-coronavirus while a third assay detected all four genera. Partial: genus scope

10.3390/pathogens9121038 Perez-Ramirez 2020: the MediLabSecure external quality assessment used this hemi-nested NS5 PCR as its recommended generic flavivirus screen; the reference lab detected all eight positive panel samples (WNV lineages 1 and 2, Usutu, JEV)
10.3390/pathogens9121038 Perez-Ramirez 2020: same external quality assessment; not independent of the round1 row

10.3390/v13112148 Guarido 2021: could not amplify the larger NS5 fragment from 12 of 17 flavivirus-positive mosquito pools, all classical insect-specific flaviviruses. Entered as partial: the gap is a virus group the mammalian-flavivirus primers were not designed for

10.3390/v13081527 Mira 2021 (first author Mira, checked against Crossref): the nested DPOL consensus PCR detected gammaherpesvirus DNA in 29/40 donkeys in a respiratory outbreak and yielded more amplicons than the parallel gB and terminase PCRs on the same samples
10.3390/v13081527 Mira 2021: same outbreak study; not independent of the round1 row

10.1093/ve/veaa024 Vaz 2020 (first author Vaz): the Wellehan pan-adenovirus nested PCR gave 83/409 Australian wild-bird samples positive, yielding 35 novel sequences across atadeno-, siadeno-, aviadeno- and mastadenoviruses
10.1093/ve/veaa024 Vaz 2020: same survey; not independent of the round1 row

10.3390/v13040641 Majumdar 2021 (first author Majumdar): the Nix VP1 typing assay typed 83 of 112 enterovirus-positive English clinical specimens with 100% serotype agreement against entire-capsid sequencing
10.3390/v13040641 Majumdar 2021: same study; not independent of the preceding row

10.1016/j.ijppaw.2019.05.002 Lotta 2019: primer HaemR2L did not match the cytochrome b of two new Leucocytozoon species with fusiform host-cell gametocytes, with mismatches at both primer ends, and none of the lineages recovered by whole-mtDNA amplification could be amplified by this protocol. The mismatch Lotta shows is in HaemR2L, the Leucocytozoon second round; this entry (HaemNFI/HaemNR3) is the shared first round of the protocol they found failing, so the row holds at the protocol level

10.3390/v11100930 Ehlers 2019 (first author Ehlers): across 1,614 samples the Johne generic VP1 PCR was used for only one host matrix while the group's own degenerate VP1 PCR was the primary screen, and species-specific nested PCRs were needed for seven further hosts. Partial: generic detection was insufficient, not absent

10.1186/s40794-020-00114-2 Fieldhouse 2020: Table 1 prints polFouter/polRouter byte-identical to the registry, cited to Wellehan 2004. On 599 nasopharyngeal swabs (Sarawak, 2017-18) the nested pol PCR gave 74 positives against 62 for a real-time AdV assay; sequencing recovered HAdV-7 and, in two patients, Desmodus rotundus adenovirus 1 at 100% identity to KX774303. NOT INDEPENDENT: this assay already has a development-set row. ONE EVENT with round2.

10.1186/s40794-020-00114-2 Fieldhouse 2020: Table 1 prints polFinner/polRinner byte-identical to the registry. The 74-of-599 figure is the nested read-out, so round 2 produced the sequenced amplicons. Caveat: a separate hexon nested PCR (Lu & Erdman 2006, not a registry entry) found 84 of 428 on its own subset, so the pol assay did not reach every hexon-positive specimen. ONE EVENT with round1.

10.1002/jmv.70389 Habeebur-Rahman 2025: Table 1 prints CoV-FWD1/CoV-RVS1 as the Quan assay; the reverse is exact and the forward identical with inosine where the registry stores N. On 346 bat faecal samples from 29 species this assay found 50 positives and a Watanabe-derived assay 44, only 18 shared (kappa 0.286), so each missed about 30 the other found. NOT INDEPENDENT: assay already in the development set. ONE EVENT with round2.

10.1002/jmv.70389 Habeebur-Rahman 2025: Table 1 prints CoV-FWD2/CoV-RVS2 byte-identical to the registry. The 50-of-346 count is the nested round-2 read-out; 26 samples called positive by the other assay were negative through the full nested protocol. Positives spanned six subgenus-level clades. NOT INDEPENDENT: assay already in the development set. ONE EVENT with round1.

10.1186/s12936-021-04019-z Harl 2022: prints HaemNFI and HaemNR3 verbatim, identical to the registry. States the nested assay does not allow amplification of the cytB of parasites of the Leucocytozoon toddi group; HaemNFI carries a 2 bp 3' mismatch and HaemR2 four mismatches to the H. elani/hBUBT1 group. 60 of 183 raptors carried toddi-group lineages recoverable only with other primers. NOT INDEPENDENT: this assay already has a development-set row (Lotta 2019). ONE EVENT with the Pan_Plasmodium row.

10.1186/s12936-021-04019-z Harl 2022: prints HaemF and HaemR2 verbatim, identical to the registry. Same finding: the second-round Leucocytozoon primers miss the toddi group, and the raptor lineages were recovered only with other primers. ONE EVENT with the Pan_hemoparasite row above.

10.1186/s12985-021-01694-x Lee 2021: primer table prints DFA and KG1 exactly as the registry stores them. In three wild-born Bornean elephant calves with fatal EEHV haemorrhagic disease, confirmed EEHV1A by a specific assay, the consensus polymerase and terminase PCRs did not detect herpesvirus in any tested sample. NOT INDEPENDENT: this assay already has a development-set row. ONE EVENT with the three sibling rows and the two pan-EEHV works rows below (same paper, same samples).
10.1186/s12985-021-01694-x Lee 2021: the table prints TGV and IYG exactly as the registry stores them. Same experiment and same negative result for the nested round. ONE EVENT with the sibling rows.

10.1186/s12985-021-01694-x Lee 2021: the table prints the terminase round-1 pair in deoxyinosine-substituted form of the registry's sequences, and again under their LGH names. Same experiment and same negative result. ONE EVENT with the sibling rows.
10.1186/s12985-021-01694-x Lee 2021: the table prints the terminase round-2 pair matching the registry. Same experiment and same negative result. ONE EVENT with the sibling rows.

10.1006/viro.1998.9207 Quackenbush 1998 Virology 246:392-399: cites VanDevanter 1996 and prints DFA/KG1/TGV/IYG; ~250 bp round-2 product sequenced from five green turtle fibropapillomas, 53% identical to BHV-1/PRV between TGV and IYG (PROPOSED, awaiting sign-off)

10.1186/s12936-021-04019-z Himmel 2022 Malar J 21:1 (PMC8729155): HaemNFI/HaemNR3 printed verbatim; the paper states the nest cannot amplify CytB of the L. toddi group, locating a two bp 3'-end mismatch in HaemNFI (AG vs GC), and screened all 183 samples again with a group-specific protocol to cover it (PROPOSED, awaiting sign-off)

10.1186/s12936-021-04019-z Himmel 2022 Malar J 21:1 (PMC8729155): HaemF/HaemR2 printed verbatim; the discussion reports four 3'-region mismatches in HaemR2 to the hBUBT1 clade and names that as the likely reason for its "extremely scarce molecular genetic record" elsewhere, the paper's own sequences for it coming from other primers (PROPOSED, awaiting sign-off)

10.5455/ovj.2024.v14.i1.48 Open Vet J 14:48 (PMC11018441), received 2023-10-01: DFA/ILK/KG1 printed verbatim as the primary mixture, cited to Van Devanter 1996; EHV-1 and EHV-4 detected and typed in Arabian horses (50% and 10% of aborted-mare vaginal swabs, 28% and 36% of nasal swabs) (PROPOSED, awaiting sign-off)

10.5455/ovj.2024.v14.i1.48 Open Vet J 14:48 (PMC11018441), received 2023-10-01: TGV plus the downstream inner primer printed as the secondary mixture; the nested product is what was typed and sequenced for EHV-1/EHV-4 (PROPOSED, awaiting sign-off)

10.1080/01652176.2022.2149879 Vet Q (PMC9809401): DFA/ILK/KG1 printed verbatim, cited to VanDevanter 1996; herpesvirus DNA confirmed in 5 of 66 pudus, four sequencing to CpHV-2 and one to a novel gammaherpesvirus 78.7% identical to fallow deer lymphotropic herpesvirus (PROPOSED, awaiting sign-off)

10.1093/ve/veab110 Virus Evol 8:veab110 (PMC8867583): CoV-FWD2/CoV-RVS2 printed verbatim in Table 1 as the nested family-level RdRp assay; CoV RNA detected in 175 bats, 1 civet and 1 shrew overall, with "the Quan PCR protocols produced 64 positive results" against 173 for the second protocol in the same samples (PROPOSED, awaiting sign-off)
